build_plan.exit_criteria: Sun body 188.507 by 186.722 by 6.2 mm with 24 blind lane pockets, an unbroken edge circle at radius 79.70 mm, 48 separate flames rooted on it with no adjacent roots touching and no closed loop anywhere, and 24 lane tiles ending on one exact arc at radius 79.55 mm with a constant 0.70 mm orange margin. Wall and overhang gates pass on all 25 parts.
30 identical 10.0 by 7.0 by 4.5 mm teardrop drops in 2 filament tones, a counter at the outermost station fully supported on its own tile, and the wall and overhang gates passing on all 30.

components.duty: Carries the 24 playable points in 4 banks of 6, each with capacity 15 counters, plus the exposed centre bar that holds every displaced drop until it recirculates.
components.form: One printed disc of radius 79.70 mm and 6.2 mm total height. Its top carries 24 blind lane pockets 1.6 mm deep on a 15 degree pitch, a rim ring dropped 0.4 mm to carry the tile lips, and a 24.0 mm centre bar standing 0.8 mm proud with 4 engraved V ticks on the 4 bank boundaries. Its edge circle is unbroken, and 48 separate curled flames stand off that circle, each rooted on its own arc of it, the tallest reaching radius 96.70 mm.
components.interfaces: 24 blind pockets receive the 24 lane tiles through a 0.15 mm clearance on each side and a 6.0 mm locating key recess per lane; the bar top at 6.2 mm receives displaced drops.
components.name: Sun board
components.placement: Flat on the table, underside down, both people reaching its face. It is the only part that is not loose.

components.duty: Marks playable point 1 in the light tone and gives that point its own seated landing surface.
components.form: One tapered sector strip 2.2 mm thick over its seat and 1.0 mm over its outer lip, spanning radius 26.5 mm to 79.55 mm, its outer edge one exact circular arc, with a 6.0 by 1.6 mm locating key under it. No notch, bay or scallop is cut into any end of it.
components.interfaces: Its key drops into the pocket recess; its lip laps the rim ring at 5.0 mm; its top carries counters at 5 radial stations.
components.name: Lane tile 1
components.placement: Seated in the lane pocket on the -75 degree axis, top at 6.0 mm, standing 0.6 mm proud of the deck.

concept.interaction: Two people each take the 15 drops of one filament tone and supply their own ordinary six-sided die cup; the pair shares two ordinary 1-6 dice of any standard make, which the set does not include. The Sun board is set between them. Each rolls both dice and moves drops the exact die distances along the lane tiles, counting the printed points in opposite directions. Landing on a point holding one enemy drop displaces it onto the centre bar, and that drop must re-enter from the opposite home bank before its owner moves anything else. The first person to drain all 15 wins.
concept.summary: Backgammon on a Sun. Two streams of condensed plasma travel 24 radial lanes, scatter lone drops onto the exposed flare at the centre, and rain back out of play. The rim is a crown of 48 separate licks of flame standing off the disc's own circular edge.
concept.title: Rainward Emberfan

baseline.note: This Make is a correction of an unreleased set. The cloned CAD supplies the construction, the plan mathematics, the rule ledger, the counter outline and the audit method. The clone's sealed parameters are an earlier link in the chain than the build the Wish restates, so the Wish's own restated values govern every carried-over dimension.

research.current_access: No network access was used in this Make. Every claim here is read from the sealed Wish, the sealed reference images, the local clone, or measured on the built geometry.

design_changes.reason: The Wish fixes no count. 48 is the largest count whose roots stay under 55 per cent of their own root-to-root arc while every valley stays under its own roots, and it is the density the concept image reads at.

design_changes.decision: the tip cap runs opposite to the flame length
design_changes.previous: the first build of this revision gave the tallest flames the widest cap
design_changes.reason: A 17 mm lick ending in a 4.10 mm cap reads as an oar. The mapping is squared, so only the shortest nubs carry the widest cap; every tip stays blunt and rounded.

design_changes.decision: the bank markers are engraved V ticks on the centre bar
design_changes.previous: the clone raised a capsule marker out among the lanes
design_changes.reason: The constant 0.70 mm orange margin the Wish fixes leaves no boundary wide enough for a raised rib that is not a wall under the checked minimum. An independent blind critic read an earlier hub-ring placement as unresolved slivers, so the mark moved to the one flat open surface that had room.

research.inventor_method: Mara Masque reskins widely popular public-domain board games with astronomy-first themes while preserving their exact rules. The 1911 Backgammon rules are carried byte for byte; only the surface is coronal rain.

reference_images.read: The concept: a plain circular disc of 24 radial lanes, teardrop counters in two tones, player-supplied cups and dice, and a rim of separate licks of flame with open background between them and notches cutting down to the disc's own edge.

The previous round's own unwrapped comparison, one third of the ring at radius 0.86 to 1.22 of the disc. Its built strip is the fault being corrected: licks fused at the root into one poured mass, with the hero arch's two legs showing as teardrop holes.

rules_ledger.note: Carried into this revision byte for byte; not edited.
